correctness.rationale: Independently eliminate lower rows to normalize the stable age vector by w_1=1. Then lambda=sum_j f_j w_j(lambda); implicit differentiation gives G_j=w_j/(1-sum_i f_i w_i'), a common positive denominator (the weights are nonincreasing functions of lambda>t). The lower-row multipliers are s_j/lambda through class n-1, and s_(n-1)/(lambda-t) at the terminal step, giving strict nonterminal descent in the stated growth regime and exactly the reported tail-product ratio. For terminal-only fertility F=lambda/w_n(lambda) increases strictly. The h_j used to compare ranks increase from 1-t to infinity on [1,infinity); equality P_j=1-t reaches replacement only. Eligible indices form a suffix, and at a crossing with j the terminal value is strictly above j+1, so that next crossing must occur later. This includes t=0 (no growing-regime crossing) and survival entries equal to one (crossings remain distinct). An independent scalar bisection reproduces the three growth and fertility crossings in the four-class example. Inspected but did not execute the frozen checker; the proof is symbolic. Absolute sensitivities and not elasticities are ranked.

value.rationale: A modest structural contribution: S2 identifies a real missing terminal comparison in a standard demographic model. The criterion distinguishes fixed-survival populations whose adult plus class can pass every absolute-sensitivity rank from those where some ranks are structurally impossible. It gives all threshold and tie conditions rather than only recomputing a sensitivity or naming an example. Its use is to interpret the terminal exception and diagnose crossings in the stated one-parameter family, not to recommend conservation interventions.
